summary: The first measured v21 mismatch occurs when C reaches weapon.c:dry_a_towel after apply.c:use_towel cleans the hero’s cream-blinded face with a carried wet towel. JavaScript records note_unported('apply.c dry_a_towel') and skips the void call, omitting the towel drying message and the wetness, wielded-state, and inventory updates. The smallest coherent source family is weapon.c:finish_towel_change, wet_a_towel, and dry_a_towel, wired at their existing source callers.

source.branch: finish_towel_change clamps changed towel wetness to 0–7, updates obj->spe, changes gu.unweapon when the hero wields the towel, and refreshes inventory for carried towels. wet_a_towel reports only an increase and dry_a_towel reports only a decrease; both finish any changed value through that helper. Feedback depends on verbose and whether the towel is carried or carried by a visible monster. This case reaches the dry branch with amt -1 after use_towel removes u.ucreamed; drying_feedback is true when the towel is uwep.
callers: apply.c:use_towel (four wet-towel cleanup branches; assigned case reaches the cream-cleanup branch)
uhitm.c:hmon_hitmon (after the hit message when hmd.dryit is set)
dothrow.c:throw_obj (before throwing a wet towel, with verbose false)
engrave.c:doengrave (when a wet towel wipes an engraving)
trap.c:burnarmor (randomly decreases a carried wet towel after fire damage)
dependencies: obj.h:is_wet_towel tests towel wetness from obj->spe
carried, mcarried, and canseemon select hero and monster feedback paths
Yobjnam2, xname, Monnam, s_suffix, and pline construct towel feedback
uwep and gu.unweapon preserve the wielded-towel state
update_inventory refreshes the carried towel description after obj->spe changes

evidence: The saved queue entry and challenges/evaluations/20261003183000-v21.json identify 3 unmatched screens of 37, 34/37 screens matched, and the first mismatch at segment 0, step 33, key n: C row 0 column 44 is “-” while JavaScript is blank. All 2,890 RNG calls match; the cursor also first diverges at step 33. The evaluation commit is b0fd76f6091376c07bf54e8d3061aa5a9c9957d0.

The manifest entry for this case says that C applies the cream pie, then applies the wet towel; cleanup reaches dry_a_towel at step 33, followed by the drying line at step 34 and the towel wetness change at step 35. The saved C65 comparison .cache/C65-qualified-current-base-comparisons-v1.json independently names weapon.c:dry_a_towel as the first mismatch behavior and records the JavaScript boundary as unported.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:use_towel (112–197), especially 173–187, removes u.ucreamed and then calls dry_a_towel(obj, -1, drying_feedback) when is_wet_towel(obj). Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/weapon.c:finish_towel_change (1018–1034), wet_a_towel (1036–1063), and dry_a_towel (1065–1088) form the contiguous source family; dry_a_towel reports a decrease and applies the new spe through the helper.

At inspected HEAD 4901dd542af51235daa15e837437a78fa6af5787, js/apply.js:4279–4304 substitutes note_unported for the source dry call, including this cream-cleanup branch. The other direct dry callers are similarly skipped in js/uhitm.js:3538–3541, js/dothrow.js:2126–2127, and js/engrave.js:673. The C wet caller is trap.c:water_damage (4712–4852); its JavaScript counterpart js/trap_water_damage.js:230 records note_unported('weapon.c wet_a_towel').

The direct C caller set also includes trap.c:burnarmor (88–160), which checks carried towels before item erosion and may dry one by a random amount. Its JavaScript counterpart js/trap_erode_obj.js:411–426 currently throws UnsupportedErosionError for a wet towel and otherwise records note_unported('apply.c dry_a_towel'), so the future source port must replace that refusal and wire this caller too. trap.c:water_damage (4712–4852) calls wet_a_towel at :4734; js/trap_water_damage.js:230 currently records note_unported('weapon.c wet_a_towel').
